fact: The westernmost star of Orion's Belt — poised almost exactly on the celestial equator.
bio: Mintaka (Delta Orionis) is a hot, massive multiple system more than a thousand light-years away, the western star of Orion's Belt. It lies so close to the celestial equator that it rises very nearly due east and sets very nearly due west for observers everywhere on Earth.
cultural: The name is Arabic for 'the belt'. As one of the three Belt stars, it shares in the near-universal recognition of Orion, and its place on the equator made it a natural marker of east and west.
